transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well… I don’t want to sound like I’m making a big fuss, doctor. But I came because people keep telling me I’m imagining things, and I don’t think I am. I’ve noticed people from the hospital, and some from the agency, watching around our house and even my cleaning routes… like they’re checking whether I’m taking proper care of my husband. I’m just trying to do the right thing, you know?
Have you been feeling unusually high, excited, or full of energy lately?

Sometimes, yes… but I wouldn’t want to make it sound dramatic. I get these stretches where I feel brighter, stronger, like I can handle everything on my own. And then if my husband or one of the clients questions me, I can snap harder than I mean to. I don’t like that about myself, but it happens.
Do you ever hear voices when no one else is there?

Um… yes, sometimes. I didn’t want to say it wrong, because I know how it sounds. But even when the house is quiet, I’ll hear a woman’s voice near the kitchen window, like she’s right there. She tells me to check the locks, or to move his pills. It’s very clear… not just a thought. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
When you hear that woman’s voice, does it happen only during those times when you feel unusually bright and strong?

Not only then, no. I mean… I wish I could say it was just when I’m all keyed up, because that would make more sense maybe. But there was a quieter stretch, a few weeks, where I was sleeping more and not rushing around so much, and I still heard her by the kitchen window. And I still felt like the agency was keeping an eye on us. Is that… is that what you’re asking?
For how long have you been hearing that woman’s voice?

I think… about eleven months, maybe close to that. I didn’t keep track exactly at first because I thought maybe it would pass, or I was just stressed. But the voice — and that feeling like people are watching us — it’s been going on most of this past year. Is that the kind of timeframe you need?
Over this past year, have you had more trouble doing your usual work or taking care of things at home than before this started?

Yes… I think so. I don’t like saying it that way, because I’ve always tried to be dependable. But my cleaning agency did take away my supervisory routes. They said clients and coworkers were saying they couldn’t count on my work the same way anymore.

And at home… I still try, I really do, but my husband and pastor have had to step in more. Some of the caregiving and house things, I haven’t been keeping up with them safely like I should. Does that answer what you mean?
During those brighter, stronger periods, do you need much less sleep than usual?

Yes… I guess I do. I don’t always think of it as a problem at the time, because I feel like I’m finally getting things done. But a lot of nights I’ll sleep maybe two or three hours, and then I wake up ready to scrub floors or sort through papers, like I’m not tired the way I normally would be. Is that what you mean?

Was there ever a stretch of at least two weeks when you were hearing the woman’s voice or felt people were watching you, but you were not feeling especially high, energized, or unusually low at the same time?

Yes… I think there was. It wasn’t as intense, so I almost didn’t count it, but there were several weeks where I was sleeping more and I wasn’t rushing around like before.

But even then, I still heard the woman’s voice by the kitchen window sometimes, and I still felt like the agency was watching us. I wasn’t especially high or low then… just quieter, I guess. Is that the kind of stretch you’re asking about?
During this past year, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I’m not sure I’d call it depressed like that… at least not for two whole weeks most of the day. I’ve had low days, and times I was quieter or worn down, but I don’t know that it was nearly every day for that long.

I don’t want to give you the wrong answer. If you mean just feeling discouraged sometimes, then yes, that happens. But the way you’re saying it—most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks—I don’t think I can say yes to that.
Before any of this started, had you been diagnosed with a medical problem affecting your brain or nervous system?

Not that I know of, no. I mean… I’ve had regular aches and things like anyone, but nobody ever told me I had something wrong with my brain or nerves before all this. At least, not that I remember. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
During those brighter, stronger periods, have you felt you had special powers or an unusually important role?

Well… I don’t know if I’d say “special powers,” exactly. That sounds a little much.

But during those times, I did feel like I was the one who could see what needed to be done. Like I had the sense and the strength to keep my husband and my home safe… and even some people from church, too. I felt like if I didn’t stay on top of it, something bad was going to happen and they needed me.

Does that make sense? I’m not trying to make it sound grand or anything.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least one week when you felt unusually high or full of energy most of the day nearly every day?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I wouldn’t want to make it sound dramatic, but there are stretches where I feel really bright and strong, like I can handle everything and keep everything together.

It can last about a week, sometimes more, where most of the day I’m just… more up, more energized. But I also get touchy then. If my husband questions me, or even a client says something like I’m doing it wrong, I can snap harder than I mean to. I don’t like that part. I’m not trying to be difficult, it just comes out fast. Does that count as what you’re asking?
During one of those week-long bright, strong periods, were you ever hospitalized because of it?

No… I don’t think I was ever hospitalized just because of those brighter, stronger spells. At least, not that I would call it that.

I mean, they could cause some trouble, but I wasn’t taken into the hospital for feeling up or energetic like that. Is that what you mean?
During one of those bright, strong periods, did it ever cause serious problems in your life?

It… it has caused some problems, yes. I don’t like saying “serious,” because that makes it sound like I just stopped caring, and I really haven’t.

But my cleaning agency did take away my supervisory routes. Clients and some coworkers said they couldn’t rely on my work the way they used to, which was embarrassing. I thought I was keeping things together, but I guess it didn’t look that way to them.

And at home… my husband has had to step in more, and even my pastor sometimes, because I haven’t been keeping up with the caregiving and house things as safely as I should. I’m trying, I really am. Is that the kind of problem you mean?

This makes F25.0 most likely; F20.0 remains possible if mood episodes are not present for a substantial portion overall; F30.2 remains as a less likely alternative if psychosis were only during mania. F22 is ruled down by prominent hallucinations and functional decline; F06.2 is ruled down by no known neurological condition.

opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions) for about 11 months, with clear evidence that these symptoms also occurred for several weeks in the absence of mood symptoms. In addition, she has had a distinct manic syndrome lasting at least one week with elevated/expansive mood, increased energy, decreased need for sleep, irritability, and inflated sense of special responsibility/importance causing significant impairment. This combination is most consistent with schizoaffective disorder, manic type, rather than schizophrenia alone or a pure manic episode with psychotic symptoms.
